query: What kinds of hardware issues appear in these incidents?

per_column.name: hardware_component
per_column.rationale: The affected component (printer, monitor, keyboard, etc.) is a genuine constitutive aspect OF a hardware issue -- the 'what part of the hardware' facet. It carves the concept along a valid dimension.

per_column.name: issue_type
per_column.rationale: The nature of the malfunction (connection issue, display issue, overheating, power/boot) is an aspect OF the hardware hiccup -- the 'what kind of failure' facet. Note some values ('Hardware Issue') are near-restatements and 'Display Issue' overlaps with the Monitor component, weakening exclusivity.

per_column.name: is_critical_hardware
per_column.rationale: A criticality/severity flag is an assessment attribute or predictor of impact, not a constitutive part of what the hardware hiccup IS. It describes importance, not an aspect of the issue itself.

judge.rationale: Two of three columns are genuine facets of a hardware hiccup: the affected component and the type/nature of failure. These are legitimate MECE-style dimensions, but mutual exclusivity is only moderate because failure-type values partly recapitulate component identity (e.g., 'Display Issue' <-> Monitor, 'Color/Print Issue' <-> Printer) and 'Hardware Issue' is a restatement of the whole. Exhaustiveness is moderate: component and failure-mode are covered, but other constitutive aspects (e.g., symptom manifestation, when-in-lifecycle it occurs, resolution type) are absent. The third column, is_critical_hardware, is a severity/importance predictor rather than a constitutive part-of facet, so it fails the meronymy test.
